description:
Define the missing-lease refusal once as a typed error, and move the lease checks of gate attach, remove, pass and fail, issue assign and unassign, and template application into the session that publishes their change, under a claims guard taken first. The lock-free pre-session check is deleted.

## Background

- The message `No active lease for issue {id}.\nAcquire lease with: jit claim acquire {id}` is formatted in `captured_lease_warnings` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:778-813`, text at `:805`) and in `require_active_lease` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:3399`, text at `:3413`); a third copy in the template lease warnings (`crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs:277-316`, text at `:306`) goes away when template warnings come from `captured_lease_warnings`. Strict mode returns the text through `anyhow!`/`bail!` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:808`, `:3420`), so callers and `crates/jit/src/output/failure.rs` can match it only by string. Error types live in `crates/jit/src/errors.rs` as `thiserror` structs (for example `LeaseNotFoundError`, `:378`). Tests assert the text: `crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs:2225` (`test_delete_issue_retries_when_lease_mode_changes_after_preflight`), `crates/jit/src/commands/gate_check.rs:3912` (`test_strict_lease_rejection_precedes_external_precheck`), `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:4306`, and `crates/jit/tests/cli_gate/gate_cli_integration_test.rs:382,397`.
- `require_active_lease` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:3399`) and `check_active_lease` (`:3339`) read lease state outside the claims lock and before the publishing session opens, with the mode taken from the executor's disk-backed configuration cache (`self.cached_config()`, `:3404`). They are called before publication by `IssueOps::assign_issue` (`issue.rs:726`, check at `:737`), `IssueOps::unassign_issue` (`issue.rs:772`, `:783`), `add_gates` (`crates/jit/src/commands/gate.rs:696`, `:715`), `remove_gates` (`gate.rs:742`, `:761`), `pass_gate` (`gate.rs:786`, `:807`) and `fail_gate` (`gate.rs:952`, `:972`). Their unit tests are at `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:4232,4259,4280,4311`.
- `pass_gate` runs an automated gate's checker through `check_gate_with` (`crates/jit/src/commands/gate_check.rs:902`) after the lease check, so today a strict unleased automated pass is refused before the checker runs. `check_gate_with` captures its inputs in one session and records the run in a second; the checker runs between them, outside the lock. Upstream, the gate-capture and verdict-reuse changes rewrite this function: the inputs capture holds only the evaluated issue's latest runs, and a reusable verdict is looked up from one verdict record (today `IssueStore::find_reusable_gate_run`, called at `gate_check.rs:964` after the inputs session). The preliminary lease check is added to the inputs session as those changes leave it, ahead of both the reuse lookup and the checker. `gate evaluate-all` reaches the same path through `pass_all_gates` (`gate.rs:890`), which calls `pass_gate` per required gate.
- The in-session form already exists: the field update takes `claims_mutation_guard` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:757`) before `open_mutation_session` and calls `captured_lease_warnings` (`:778`) with the captured mode and issues (`publish_captured_field_update`, `:2599`). The guard is `None` outside a git repository, so warn mode warns and strict mode refuses (`@/charter/D-4`).
- The lifecycle path keeps a preliminary captured check: it refuses a strict unleased transition with a preliminary guard over the preflight image before running prechecks, and repeats the check under the held guard when publishing (`publish_captured_lifecycle_mutation`, `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2840-2860`; owning test `test_strict_lease_rejection_precedes_external_precheck`, `gate_check.rs:3868`). That refusal is part of the publishing operation and stays. The dedicated commands publish through `publish_captured_issue_mutation` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2298`; `SetManualGateStatus` for manual pass and fail, `:493`).
- `apply_template_request` (`template.rs:152`) opens a first session (`:170-191`) only to derive the lease targets and mode, computes warnings between sessions (`template_lease_warnings`, `:193`, defined `:277`; upstream lock-free reader work routes this through the guarded check `captured_lease_warnings`), then opens a second session, re-derives, and retries if the targets or mode changed (`:200-219`); the claims guard is not held across publication. `DerivedTemplateApply::lease_targets` (`template.rs:320`) and `existing_template_lease_targets` (`:265`) already name the existing issues the apply edits.
- Lock order: the claims guard must be taken before any repository session. `issue assign` and `issue unassign` (`IssueCommands::coordinates_claims_first`, `crates/jit/src/cli.rs:2915`) and `gate add`, `gate remove`, `gate evaluate`, `gate evaluate-all`, `gate evaluate-many` and `gate fail` (`GateCommands::coordinates_claims_first`, `cli.rs:2948`) are classified repository-first and need recovery dispatch (`GateCommands::requires_recovery_dispatch`, `cli.rs:2781-2800`), so `open_repository` opens a startup session for them (`crates/jit/src/commands/bootstrap.rs:102-124`, called from `crates/jit/src/main.rs:1637`), and a claims guard taken afterwards is refused by the guard-order check (`crates/jit/src/storage/guard_order.rs`). `jit apply` is repository-first likewise (`Commands::coordinates_claims_first`, `cli.rs:2697`, the `Self::Apply` arm at `:2722`); `gate preset apply` is already claims-first. `CLAIM_FIRST_LEAF_COMMANDS` (`cli.rs:3236`) and `test_claim_first_classification_covers_exact_cli_callers` (`cli.rs:3331`) pin the classification.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `crates/jit/src/errors.rs` defines `LeaseRequiredError` naming the issue, and its `Display` is the only place the missing-lease message text is written; in strict mode every lease check returns an error that downcasts to `LeaseRequiredError`, in warn mode it pushes the rendered `Display` as the warning; a unit test asserts the strict downcast (it fails today) and the existing message assertions pass unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-02: `require_active_lease` and `check_active_lease` no longer exist; assign, unassign, gate attach and removal, manual pass, manual fail and automated pass check the target issue's lease through `captured_lease_warnings` inside the session that publishes their change, holding the claims guard taken before that session. A harness test shows strict mode refusing an unleased assign with `LeaseRequiredError` while leaving the stored issue unchanged, warn mode returning the warning with the assignment applied, and a strict unleased automated pass refused in `check_gate_with`'s inputs session with no run of a checker that records its invocation.
- [hard] REQ-03: Template application takes the claims guard before its one publishing session and checks the captured lease targets with `captured_lease_warnings` inside that session, with no session that only computes lease targets; a harness test counting session opens shows one session per successful apply attempt (today two), and strict mode refuses an apply that edits an unleased existing issue without publishing anything.
- [hard] REQ-04: `issue assign`, `issue unassign`, `gate add`, `gate remove`, `gate evaluate`, `gate evaluate-all`, `gate evaluate-many`, `gate fail` and `jit apply` are classified claims-first, and the classification inventory test lists them (this assertion fails today).

## Notes

- Behaviour change: assign, unassign and the gate commands now read the lease under the claims lock and the mode from the captured configuration; outside a git repository, warn mode warns and strict mode refuses instead of failing on worktree-path resolution. The lifecycle path's preliminary refusal before prechecks is unchanged, and postcheck-driven automated passes are system-derived and check no lease.
- Behaviour change: template application reads the lease under the claims lock in the publishing session and `jit apply` locks claims before the repository; the warnings and refusals are otherwise unchanged.
- The missing-lease warning and error text stay byte-identical and the process exit status is unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.


## Superseded by 17fbcf25

17fbcf25 replaced the lease rule this issue describes. Strict mode now refuses only when anyone other than the writer holds an active lease, through `ClaimsIndex::conflicting_lease` and `refuse_foreign_leases`, with a table-driven test over every command. `require_active_lease` and `check_active_lease` are gone, and a mutation with no lease on an unleased issue succeeds. Read this issue's criteria against that rule: they must use `conflicting_lease`, and the missing-lease message and "strict refuses unleased" assertions no longer apply. Moving the checks into the publishing session under a claims guard remains a valid direction.
title: Dedicated, gate and template writes check their leases in their publishing session
